findings.statement: Target's gross margin fell 4.64 percentage points in fiscal 2022, which was dramatically worse than the peer median decline of ~0.85 pp (WMT -0.96, COST -0.74, DG -0.37, BBY -1.08 pp; DLTR improved +2.14 pp), indicating the margin compression was overwhelmingly company-specific rather than sector-wide.
Target's cost of sales grew 9.69% year-over-year in fiscal 2022 while revenue grew only 2.94%, a 6.75 percentage-point gap that drove the gross margin decline from 29.28% to 24.64%.

BLS retail-margin PPIs (dept_store_margins and grocery_margins) both rose during fiscal 2022, meaning sector-wide retailers were earning MORE margin per unit sold, not less—contradicting a sector-wide margin compression narrative and reinforcing that Target's decline was idiosyncratic.

Target's operating margin fell 4.91 pp vs gross margin's 4.64 pp decline (only 0.27 pp worse), and inventory decreased 2.9% while revenue rose 2.9%, indicating no significant shrinkage or inventory write-off signal beyond normal SG&A pressure.

Financial_fact XBRL data for Target shows only aggregated revenue and cost_of_sales tags (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold) with no category-level gross profit breakdown available, preventing isolation of discretionary vs. essential category mix effects.
